primary_task: Design a Kubernetes platform architecture with GitOps, for example "Design a multi-cluster Kubernetes platform with GitOps for a financial services company", delivered as architecture and configuration (manifests, Helm/Kustomize, ArgoCD/Flux definitions).

requirements.name: kubernetes-config-tooling (helm/kustomize/kubectl/argocd/flux)
requirements.evidence: "**Kubernetes-native IaC**: Helm 3.x, Kustomize, Jsonnet, cdk8s, Pulumi Kubernetes provider"; "**GitOps tools**: ArgoCD, Flux v2". Writing these files is text; running the CLIs is not required by the document.
requirements.basis: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads)"

requirements.name: managed-kubernetes-cloud-account (EKS/AKS/GKE/OKE)
requirements.evidence: "**Managed Kubernetes**: EKS (AWS), AKS (Azure), GKE (Google Cloud), OKE (OCI)" -- only needed if the platform is actually provisioned, which the design request does not ask.
requirements.basis: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP, ...)"

requirements.name: docker
requirements.evidence: "**Container runtimes**: containerd, CRI-O, Docker runtime considerations"; "**Image optimization**: Multi-stage builds" (knowledge areas, not required steps)
requirements.basis: "a Docker daemon (docker, docker compose and container builds cannot run)"

requirements.name: terraform/opentofu
requirements.basis: egress_allow lists "releases.hashicorp.com"; provider downloads from "registry.terraform.io" are in egress_deny, so terraform init/apply would fail.

notes: The document is an agent persona with a design-oriented response approach and no 'must run' step, so the representative request is a design and config-writing task. Other reading: if 'Implement GitOps workflows' / 'Set up observability stack' means deploying to a real cluster, a cluster is needed: managed clusters need cloud credentials (unavailable) and local kind/minikube need a Docker daemon (unavailable), so the verdict would be BLOCKED on credential:managed-kubernetes-cloud-account (or program:docker). Unknown: whether k3s or similar can run without Docker in the session (would need to check privileges).
